changelog:
Sixteen things found by walking the configuration page, and two of them change how the page works rather than how it looks. **The schedule now waits for Save like everything else.** Until now a schedule edit was written to the server the instant you made it, which is why moving or removing a programme never lit the Save button up - there was nothing waiting to save, it had already happened, and there was no way back from a mis-drop. Schedule edits are now held with the rest of your changes: the grid draws what they come to, Undo takes the last one back, Discard throws them all away, and one Save writes the configuration and the schedule together. What an edit does to the programmes around it is still worked out by the server, because only the server knows - dropping something on top of a film trims it, or cuts it in two - so what you are shown before you save is computed the same way as what gets stored. **And a channel's schedule can now be longer than a week**, up to thirteen: a fortnightly film cannot be said in seven days however the seven days are arranged. The grid draws one week of the cycle at a time with a picker that says which week is on air, counted from a fixed Monday so a restart cannot swap it over. Shortening a schedule keeps the first weeks and drops the rest rather than laying them on top of each other.

The rest: drop-down menus were unreadable white on white, because a translucent colour that is right on this page is composited by the browser on its own light ground when the list opens. Dragging a programme now snaps flush against the end of the one before it, the start of the one after, or a quarter hour - there was snapping before, of five minutes, which at a week's zoom is less than a pixel and so could not be seen - and the line it will land on is drawn while you drag, with Alt to place it freely and a box to type the exact day and time. Programmes on the timeline are outlined so a run of them reads as programmes rather than one long block. A selection can be let go by clicking anywhere that is not a programme, instead of only on the grid; and an item in the content list could not be unselected at all if the click drifted a pixel and became a drag. A YouTube playlist put on the shelf is now one entry that opens like a series - drag the whole thing and it lays the videos out one after another, or open it and take one video - instead of emptying forty rows onto the shelf. The picture gallery never asked an online provider at all; it now has a library half and an online half, library first, and nothing reaches out until you ask it to. Pictures are drawn larger when there are fewer of them. Every box you can type in shares one look, and a link pasted into a search box is recognised as a link rather than searched for. "Not that" on the new-channel screen cycles through other lineups again, keeping the titles and genres you gave it, instead of clearing everything; the similarity slider puts titles back when you widen it again; a channel made from nothing opens on its own empty week rather than on whichever screen you left last; and the page no longer scrolls when there is nothing below.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
